articles.title: BII Commits $65 Million to Expand Sustainable Finance in Zambia and Zimbabwe
articles.summary:
British International Investment (BII) is committing $65 million across Zambia and Zimbabwe as the UK development finance institution expands its focus on frontier markets. The financing combines investments in sustainable […]
The post BII Commits $65 Million to Expand Sustainable Finance in Zambia and Zimbabwe appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
BII Commits $65 Million to Expand Sustainable Finance in Zambia and Zimbabwe
- British International Investment is committing $65 million across Zambia and Zimbabwe as it launches its new five-year strategy in Zambia.
- A $15 million anchor investment will support Zanaco’s debut $100 million Sustainability Bond Programme, Zambia’s first bank-issued sustainability bond.
- A further $50 million will expand agriculture finance in Zimbabwe, while Horizon Zambia will help businesses prepare for private investment.
British International Investment (BII) is committing $65 million across Zambia and Zimbabwe as the UK development finance institution expands its focus on frontier markets.
The financing combines investments in sustainable capital markets and agricultural finance with technical assistance designed to address barriers to private investment.
BII announced the commitments alongside the Zambia launch of its new five-year strategy. The institution is targeting stronger local financial markets and greater private capital participation in productive sectors.
UK Minister for International Development Kirsty McNeill said: “British International Investment shows how the UK is moving from donor to investor, using our capital and expertise to unlock opportunities that can attract even more private investment. BII’s new investments in Zambia and Zimbabwe demonstrate its ongoing commitment to frontier markets, helping these countries to grow and prosper in the long-term. This will create jobs and support climate-resilient agriculture, renewable energy, and women-owned businesses, while helping to create future trade opportunities for the UK.”
Zambia’s First Bank-Issued Sustainability Bond
In Zambia, BII is making a $15 million anchor commitment to Zanaco’s debut $100 million Sustainability Bond Programme.
The programme will deliver Zambia’s first sustainability bond issued by a bank. It is designed to demonstrate how domestic capital markets can finance projects with measurable environmental and social benefits.
Proceeds will support climate-resilient agriculture, renewable energy, SMEs, women-owned businesses and critical social infrastructure.
Around 40% of the capital is expected to come from non-development finance institution investors. That participation could help broaden Zambia’s sustainable finance market and establish a precedent for future issuances.
BII has worked with Zanaco on the programme since 2023. Its technical assistance has focused on the bank’s sustainable finance framework, green financing pipeline, and environmental and social standards.
RELATED ARTICLE: British International Investment, CIP Launch $300 Million India Renewables Platform
$50 Million Targets Zimbabwe’s Agriculture Financing Gap
BII is also providing a combined $50 million facility to Central Africa Building Society and NMB Bank under its Zimbabwe Agriculture Finance Programme.
Agriculture remains central to Zimbabwe’s employment, exports and food security. However, businesses across the sector often struggle to secure long-term capital and trade finance.
The programme combines long-term lending with trade finance. Businesses will be able to finance productive assets and import equipment and other essential inputs.
Technical assistance will also support stronger environmental, social and climate risk management within Zimbabwe’s banking sector.
The structure is intended to address financing constraints while strengthening the capacity of domestic financial institutions to serve agricultural businesses.
Horizon Zambia Targets Investment Readiness
BII is pairing its financial commitments with Horizon Zambia, a country-focused programme targeting broader barriers to investment.
The initiative will provide technical assistance to help businesses become investment-ready. It will also help investors identify opportunities through policy engagement and strategic partnerships.
A pilot launched last year supported 15 SMEs and helped facilitate $8 million of investment.
Horizon Zambia joins similar BII programmes in Sierra Leone, Nepal and Ghana. BII also operates the Africa Resilience Investment Accelerator across multiple frontier markets.
Chris Chijiutomi, Managing Director and Head of Africa, British International Investment, added: “Our investments in Zambia and Zimbabwe demonstrate how we are putting our new strategy into action in frontier markets. Through partnerships with local financial institutions and targeted technical assistance, we are expanding access to long-term finance, strengthening capital markets and helping businesses invest, trade and grow. By doing so, we aim to create the conditions for more private capital to follow.”
For investors and executives, the package shows how development finance is increasingly being used to build markets rather than fund individual projects alone. Local banks, capital-market instruments and technical assistance all form part of that strategy.
If successful, the programmes could create a larger pipeline of investable businesses and sustainable assets. That matters beyond Zambia and Zimbabwe as development institutions seek models capable of drawing more private capital into frontier economies.

articles.summary:
A coalition backed by major cargo owners including Microsoft and PepsiCo has placed the largest electric Class 8 truck order in U.S. history. The deal could nearly double the country’s […]
The post Microsoft, PepsiCo Back Record 2,500-Truck Tesla Semi Order appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
Microsoft, PepsiCo Back Record 2,500-Truck Tesla Semi Order
- ZET SCALE has placed an initial order for 2,500 battery-electric Class 8 trucks, the largest electric truck order in U.S. history.
- Tesla was selected as the primary manufacturer, with Kenworth, RIDE and Volvo named as secondary suppliers for participating carriers.
- The alliance plans to scale the procurement model to at least 10,000 electric trucks, using pooled demand and leasing to reduce financial risk.
A coalition backed by major cargo owners including Microsoft and PepsiCo has placed the largest electric Class 8 truck order in U.S. history. The deal could nearly double the country’s existing electric heavy-duty truck fleet.
Smart Freight Centre and Catalyst Mobility facilitated the initial order for 2,500 battery-electric trucks through their joint ZET SCALE initiative. Tesla was selected as the primary manufacturer following a competitive procurement process.
The deal puts corporate freight demand at the center of efforts to accelerate heavy-duty transport electrification. It also introduces a financing structure designed to address one of the biggest barriers facing fleet operators: the financial risk of switching to new technology.
Pooling demand to cut costs
ZET SCALE, short for Zero-Emission Truck Shipper-Carrier Alliance Leading Electrification, pools demand from cargo owners and carriers. The approach gives manufacturers visibility into larger order volumes and allows participating companies to negotiate at scale.
Microsoft and PepsiCo are among the alliance’s founding shippers.
“Microsoft is working to turn our sustainability commitments into operational reality. Our participation in ZET SCALE does that for road freight, by signaling real demand for electric trucks so the low-carbon option becomes competitive for moving our cloud infrastructure,” said Nico De Golia, Director of Sustainability for Cloud Supply Chain Global Operations at Microsoft.
Tesla emerged as the primary original equipment manufacturer after an evaluation of price, range, charging capability and production capacity.
Kenworth, RIDE and Volvo were selected as secondary manufacturers. Carriers can use those suppliers when their operating requirements call for different vehicle specifications.
Tesla Semi Lead Dan Priestly said the size of the procurement could help accelerate adoption.
“Going big. This will help shippers adopt the Tesla Semi in volume and lower costs,” Priestly posted on LinkedIn.
RELATED ARTICLE: Microsoft Signs Long-Term Washington Solar PPA
Financing model shifts fleet risk
The alliance is also tackling the balance-sheet challenges associated with electric truck deployment.
Strategic partner ZET Financial is issuing the purchase order for the initial 2,500 trucks. It will deploy the vehicles through its ZET Lease program.
The fair market value leasing structure aims to remove residual value risk from fleet balance sheets. That risk can make electric trucks difficult to finance because their long-term resale values remain less established than diesel vehicles.
“Every part of the freight industry wants cleaner trucks, but until now each company faced that transition — and its risks — alone. ZET SCALE aligns shippers, carriers, manufacturers and financiers around a single, real demand signal. When the risk is shared across the whole chain instead of resting on any one player, the industry can finally move at scale,” said Christoph Wolff, CEO of Smart Freight Centre.
Ten U.S. freight hubs targeted
The trucks will operate across ten major freight hubs. Deployment areas include Southern California and Los Angeles, Northern California and Stockton, and Central California and Bakersfield.
Other locations include Seattle and Tacoma, Houston, Dallas, San Antonio, Chicago, Atlanta and the Northern New Jersey, Newark and New York City freight corridor.
The geographic spread could provide a significant test of electric heavy-duty trucking across different routes, climates and charging environments.
The alliance has not disclosed the official value of the transaction. California incentive program pricing lists Tesla Semi variants at approximately $260,000 to $290,000. Actual fleet pricing may differ substantially because of volume discounts, incentives and commercial terms.
ZET SCALE targets 10,000 electric trucks
ZET SCALE plans to expand its procurement model to 10,000 or more electric trucks. It is seeking additional shippers and carriers for future deployment rounds.
For corporate sustainability leaders, the model extends decarbonization efforts beyond direct operations and into freight networks. Transport emissions remain a significant challenge for companies seeking to reduce value-chain emissions.
The structure could also provide a template for other hard-to-abate sectors. Instead of individual companies absorbing technology and financing risks independently, buyers aggregate demand while carriers, manufacturers and financiers share execution risk.
If ZET SCALE reaches its 10,000-truck target, the initiative could influence how large corporate buyers use procurement power to accelerate low-carbon infrastructure and equipment. Its first 2,500-truck order will test whether aggregated demand can turn corporate climate commitments into commercially scalable freight deployment.

articles.title: J.P. Morgan, Paraguay Launch $200 Million Sustainable Forestry Investment
articles.summary:
The Office of the President of Paraguay and J.P. Morgan Natural Capital have announced an approximately $200 million investment in the country’s forestry sector. The project aims to combine sustainable […]
The post J.P. Morgan, Paraguay Launch $200 Million Sustainable Forestry Investment appeared first on ESG News.
articles.full_text:
J.P. Morgan, Paraguay Launch $200 Million Sustainable Forestry Investment
- $200 million investment: J.P. Morgan Natural Capital plans to develop a large-scale sustainable forestry platform in Paraguay, with capital deployment expected from early 2027.
- Forestry and carbon focus: The platform will combine commercial forestry, native forest restoration, carbon credits and sustainable timber production.
- Local value creation: The partners plan to process timber in Paraguay, supporting industrial development, rural employment and higher-value exports.
The Office of the President of Paraguay and J.P. Morgan Natural Capital have announced an approximately $200 million investment in the country’s forestry sector. The project aims to combine sustainable land management with industrial development and rural job creation.
Announced at the Paraguay Investment Forum NYC 2026, the investment will establish a large-scale sustainable forestry platform. It will be developed with Grupo Robinson, a Paraguayan business group active in agriculture and forestry.
Capital deployment is expected to begin in early 2027.
Building a forestry and carbon platform
The investment will focus on establishing commercial forests alongside the restoration of native forests.
The platform is also designed to generate several potential revenue streams. These include high-quality timber, carbon credits and wood products produced through sustainable forestry operations.
J.P. Morgan Natural Capital will bring international investment and natural capital expertise to the project. Grupo Robinson will contribute local knowledge, production capabilities and experience in Paraguay’s agricultural and forestry sectors.
“This investment in Paraguay is a compelling opportunity to build a scalable, long-term forestry platform grounded in sustainable resource management and rural development,” said Angela Davis, CEO of J.P. Morgan Natural Capital. “We are pleased to partner with Grupo Robinson on bringing this impactful initiative to life.”
The scale of the investment also puts carbon markets alongside traditional forestry products within the project’s commercial model. That creates exposure to both physical timber markets and emerging demand for nature-based carbon assets.
Paraguay targets more domestic processing
The partners also intend to use the forestry platform to support Paraguay’s industrialization strategy.
Rather than focusing solely on the production and export of raw materials, the initiative aims to process more timber domestically. That could allow greater economic value to remain within the country while supporting finished products for local and international markets.
For Paraguay, the project therefore extends beyond forestry investment. It links natural resource management with rural economic development, manufacturing and export potential.
“This announcement reflects Paraguay’s commitment to creating quality opportunities outside our major cities—building stronger rural communities while stewarding our natural resources responsibly,” said Santiago Peña, President of the Republic of Paraguay. “We welcome long-term partners who invest with a focus on sustainable development, job creation, and adding value in Paraguay.”
The government expects the project to create quality employment in rural areas and strengthen local communities. Its development model combines international capital with domestic expertise and locally available natural resources.
RELATED ARTICLE: J.P. Morgan Asset Management Launches Three New Sustainable ETFs
Natural capital moves closer to industrial strategy
For investors, the transaction shows how natural capital strategies are expanding beyond conservation-focused investments.
Forestry assets can generate returns through timber and wood products while creating additional opportunities through carbon markets and ecosystem restoration. However, execution will depend on credible forest management, carbon integrity and the ability to build local processing capacity.
Those factors will also determine the project’s broader ESG impact. Large-scale forestry investment can create jobs and support restoration, but governance around land use, biodiversity and community impacts remains central to long-term performance.
The Paraguay project will test whether these objectives can be integrated at commercial scale.
For corporate leaders and institutional investors, the $200 million commitment also illustrates the growing connection between natural capital and national economic development. Emerging markets with significant natural resources are increasingly looking to attract investment that does more than extract or export commodities.
Paraguay’s approach is to pair sustainable forestry with domestic processing, rural development and higher-value production.
If successful, the platform could offer a model for how international capital can support nature-based assets while building local industrial capacity. Its significance will ultimately depend on execution, particularly as investment begins in 2027 and the forestry platform moves from capital commitment to long-term production and restoration.
